title: Human Reproduction
hook: New human life begins when two specialized cells — one egg, one sperm — combine, merging half a set of genetic instructions from each parent into a brand-new whole.
key_points: Reproduction makes new individuals; in humans it is sexual, combining two parents' genes.
Sex cells (gametes) — sperm and egg — each carry half the normal set of chromosomes.
Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm and an egg, forming a single cell called a zygote.
The zygote carries a complete, unique genome and can grow into a new individual.
content_html: Reproduction is how a species makes new members of itself. Humans reproduce sexually, meaning a new individual gets genetic material from two parents. The whole process hinges on a special kind of cell built for exactly one purpose: passing on genes.
extra_html: Those special cells are the gametes — sperm from the male and the egg from the female. Unlike ordinary body cells, each gamete carries only half the normal set of chromosomes, produced by a special kind of cell division (meiosis). That halving is the clever part: when a sperm and egg meet in fertilization and fuse, the two halves combine into one complete genome — a single cell called a zygote with a full, unique set of instructions. That one cell can then divide and grow into an entire person. Khan Academy's walkthrough of meiosis explains how the gametes get their half-sets in the first place, setting the stage for fertilization.

related.title: From Embryo to Baby
related.hook: A single fertilized cell becomes trillions of specialized ones in nine months — dividing, folding, and organizing itself into a heartbeat, a brain, and a body ready to be born.

related.title: Hormones and the Endocrine System
related.hook: Your body runs a chemical messaging service: glands release hormones into the blood, and far-off organs read them like instructions — slow signals that shape growth, mood, and metabolism.

flashcards.back_html: The fusion of a sperm and an egg into a single cell called a zygote — the first cell of a new individual.

flashcards.prompt: Why do sex cells carry only half the usual number of chromosomes?

choices.text: So that combining egg and sperm restores the full, normal set
Because they are damaged versions of normal cells
Because they don't need genetic information

flashcards.explanation_html: Each gamete carries half a genome. When egg and sperm join, the halves combine into one complete set — half from each parent.

flashcards.prompt: What are the two human sex cells (gametes)?
flashcards.explanation_html: The gametes are the sperm (from the male) and the egg (from the female), the only cells that fuse to start a new individual.
